title: TOML path silently loses the frontier-review guarantee
description:
BLOCKER, finding 1 of the final review, reproduced with one config expressed both ways.

readRoutings roleFor(name) falls back to roles.implement for EVERY unlisted role, so review_model, closeout_model and scout_model can never be absent on the TOML path. Two fail-closed guards become dead code: runner.ts:1576 ("requires a valid configured review_model; no default model is accepted for final process gates") and planning.ts:1320-1321 ("scout_model is required").

With [roles.plan] opus:max and [roles.implement] haiku:low and no review/closeout/scout role:
  markdown path: review_model undefined -> run BLOCKED; scout_model undefined -> planning blocked
  TOML path:     review_model haiku:low -> THE FINAL REVIEW RUNS ON THE ECONOMY IMPLEMENT MODEL

A repo that migrates and does not add [roles.review] gets a quietly under-powered final review with no warning. This is precisely the "two paths cannot drift in fail-closed semantics" the epic set out to guarantee, and it breaks agent-runner.mds REVIEWER-TIER RULE (review with a model at least as capable as the one that wrote the code; epic final reviews default to frontier).

Fix: on the TOML path resolve review_model/closeout_model/scout_model ONLY from an explicit [roles.review]/[roles.closeout]/[roles.scout], leaving them undefined otherwise so the existing guards keep firing. Fallback-to-implement is right for tk herd spawn and wrong for the gates the pi extension refuses to default.

Also fix the related doc error: pi-runner.md says closeout falls back to the PLANNER model when [roles.closeout] is absent; on the TOML path it falls back to IMPLEMENT, and modelForTiers closeout_model ?? planner_model is unreachable there.

acceptance_criteria: With no [roles.review], the TOML path leaves review_model undefined and the run is blocked exactly as the markdown path blocks it; the same holds for scout_model and closeout_model; a test asserts parity of the fail-closed outcome between the two paths; pi-runner.md describes the actual fallback.
